entry.description: The period-index conjecture is false for motivic reasons. Version 2 gives characteristic-zero and positive-characteristic counterexamples under explicit transcendence-degree conditions, and proves a corrected Hodge-theoretic counterpart. A flawed ChatGPT example inspired the author's final construction; ChatGPT later assisted literature searches and lattice calculations. The author wrote the paper and retains responsibility.
entry.anchor_claim: The current paper reports: For any integer $d \geq 3$ and any algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $0$ and transcendence degree at least $d-3$, or of characteristic $p>2$ and transcendence degree at least $d-2$, we construct a $d$-dimensional variety over $k$ with a Brauer class of period $2$ and index $2^d$, violating the period-index conjecture; in particular, the period-index conjecture fails in dimension $3$ over $\overline{\mathbf{Q}}$ and $\overline{\mathbf{F}_p(t)}$, and in all dimensions $d \geq 3$ over $\mathbf{C}$ and $\overline{\mathbf{F}_p((t))}$. To bound the index of Brauer classes from below, we employ an obstruction of motivic nature, which requires proving the nonexistence of integral Hodge or Tate classes satisfying a certain equation modulo $2$. Motivated by these counterexamples, we propose a period-index conjecture with corrections at small primes and, as evidence, prove its Hodge-theoretic counterpart.
entry.prior_rationale: Colliot-Thelene first raised the precise period-index bound in print in 2001, after related work on period and index stretching back through the twentieth century.
entry.advance_rationale: The explicit threefold with period 2 and index 8 disproves the unramified conjecture, and a bootstrapping construction gives counterexamples to the function-field conjecture in every dimension at least 4.
entry.scope_rationale: For d>=3: characteristic zero requires transcendence degree at least d-3; characteristic p>2 requires at least d-2. The revised claim also includes the paper's stated corrected Hodge-theoretic result.
entry.resistance_rationale: The conjecture accumulated independent approaches through surfaces, unramified classes, abelian varieties, products of elliptic curves, hyperkahler varieties, and Hodge-theoretic obstructions before this counterexample.
entry.age_rationale: Elapsed duration is computed from the coded framing and solution dates; it is not a capability claim.

entry.description: riemann-zeta, primitive-dirichlet-l and xi-prime zero proportions. an unreleased research version of claude developed an unconditional pair-correlation and hermitian-form argument whose optimized test families raise the lower bounds to 0.6725 for distinct and simple critical-line zeta zeros, 0.83625 for distinct zeta zeros overall, 0.85838 for simple xi-prime zeros on the critical line, and 0.92919 for distinct xi-prime zeros overall; a quartic variant gives 0.86864 and 0.93432 for the latter two proportions. the paper's theorem b states that the theorem a zeta proportions, including the optimized constants, hold verbatim for l(s,chi) for every fixed primitive dirichlet character chi. ralph furman and levent alpöge independently re-derived and checked the argument, and the public lean 4 companion reports formalizations of theorems a and b, the montgomery-taylor variants, and six xi-prime comparator statements. an organizationally independent riemann labs workflow reports a fresh v1.0 build, axiom audit, exact comparator matching and kernel replay for those formal statements; this is formal-statement verification, not external analytic peer review. symbolic checks cover the main constants. the august 13 replacement paper restricts lemma 3.2 to the c=2 form used in the proof and leaves the recorded bounds unchanged. Independent support: Lamzouri v2 gives a different unconditional proof of the 0.67250... simple-critical-line and 0.83625... distinct-overall Riemann-zeta bounds, replacing the finite-dimensional Hermitian-matrix argument by a Hilbert-space inequality and an unconditional pair-correlation theorem. Its additional human-derived 88.76% union and 83.62% average estimates are outside this AI-result package. The independent support does not cover the record's fixed-primitive-Dirichlet-L or xi-prime extensions. No downloaded proof or formal artifact was executed in this audit.
entry.anchor_claim: Unconditionally, the optimized test families give liminf proportions at least 0.6725 for distinct and simple critical-line zeros of the Riemann zeta function and 0.83625 for distinct zeta zeros overall. The same zeta proportion bounds hold verbatim for L(s,χ) for every fixed primitive Dirichlet character χ. For xi-prime they give at least 0.85838 for simple critical-line zeros and 0.92919 for distinct zeros overall, improved by the quartic variant to 0.86864 and 0.93432 respectively.
entry.prior_rationale: The paper targets documented lower-bound frontiers for zeta zeros and the corresponding xi-prime zero-proportion problems.
entry.advance_rationale: The theorem materially raises the unconditional lower bounds for both zeta and xi-prime zero proportions and extends the zeta constants verbatim to every fixed primitive Dirichlet character but does not prove the Riemann hypothesis or determine the sharp proportions.
entry.scope_rationale: The claims are asymptotic lower bounds as the zero height tends to infinity, so they apply over unbounded families of height windows.
entry.resistance_rationale: Independent Levinson-mollifier refinements and the Montgomery pair-correlation program produced a long sequence of published attacks and successive records on these zero-proportion targets.

entry.description: kato conjecture for positive commutators. frank and ivanisvili prove that i[arctan(P),arctan(Q)] is nonnegative and nonzero, indeed trace class with trace pi/2, while arctan lacks the strip membership required by the conjectured converse, giving a counterexample. the paper acknowledges ai tools but does not identify any model or material task; the authors state that they wrote and checked all final arguments and proofs. published provisionally pending more specific ai-attribution evidence.
entry.anchor_claim: The paper reports that i[arctan(P),arctan(Q)] is a nonnegative, nonzero trace-class operator with trace pi/2, while the arctangent functions fail the strip condition required by the conjectured converse, so the Kato conjecture is false.
